title: Stale PEP 698 comment orphaned in the harness root after the #729 split
detail: tests/conformance.rs:714-719 claimed a byte-for-byte PEP 698 fixture 'is not possible until import support lands (v0.4)' and pointed at tests/issue_432_inheritance.rs, while tests/conformance/classes.rs:277 registers and runs pep_0698_override_matches_cpython_3_14_7_byte_for_byte against tests/fixtures/pep_0698_override.py. The comment was already stale on origin/main (line 930); the split left it in the root with no adjacent test.
resolution: Replaced the six-line block with a three-line pointer naming the fixture test and its cohort file. Audited every other root comment for references to moved tests: the remaining PEP mentions (695 at line 541, 649/749 at 568) belong to pep_0695_generics and pep_0613_typealias, which stay in the root; no other stale pointer found.

title: every_harness_module_on_disk_is_declared lacked the is_file guard the harness readers apply
detail: tests/conformance.rs's on-disk filter was `.filter(|path| path.extension().is_some_and(|ext| ext == "rs"))`, while tests/harness_support/conformance_sources.rs:44 and scripts/check_conformance_breadth.py:223 both require `is_file()`. A directory named `*.rs` under tests/conformance/ would be demanded by the control test but concatenated by neither reader.
resolution: Extracted the scan into `harness_modules_on_disk(dir: &Path)` with `path.is_file() &&` added to the filter, and pinned it with a ScratchDir test (`harness_modules_on_disk_ignores_directories_and_non_rs_files`) that plants a directory named fake.rs, a nested py30/ directory, a .py file, and two .rs files and asserts only the two files are returned, sorted.
